sections.label: Infectious Diseases Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Infectious Diseases Act in three areas: surveillance, preventing disease introduction, and strengthening control within Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Infectious Diseases Act (IDA) was enacted in 1976 and was last amended in 2008.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As part of our continual efforts to ensure that infectious disease prevention and control measures remain effective, this Infectious Diseases (Amendment) Bill seeks to amend the IDA in the three key areas of (a) enhancing infectious disease surveillance; (b) preventing the introduction of infectious diseases into Singapore; and lastly, (c) strengthening infectious disease control within Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Last year, my Ministry invited the public to provide their feedback on the proposed amendments over a six-week period.

sections.label: Yellow Fever specified disease
sections.summary: Yellow Fever, a serious viral infection, is the only disease specified under this section, guided by the International Health Regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To date, the only disease specified under this section, as guided by the International Health Regulations, is Yellow Fever, a serious viral infection.

sections.label: Unvaccinated travellers numbers
sections.summary: The number of travellers without the required Yellow Fever vaccination has been small, averaging 50 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The number of travellers without the required Yellow Fever vaccination has been small, at an average of 50 per year.

sections.label: Clause 13 entry refusal
sections.summary: Clause 13 allows refusal of entry of unvaccinated non-citizen travellers without first providing vaccination, isolation or surveillance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 13 of the Bill, therefore, introduces additional flexibility to allow the refusal of entry of unvaccinated non-citizen travellers without needing to first provide vaccination, isolation or surveillance.

sections.label: Clause 15 traveller surveillance
sections.summary: Clause 15 transfers the Regulation into the Act via new sections 45A and 45B, allowing medical examination and surveillance of travellers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As we recognise that these are basic and important means of preventing and controlling infectious diseases, clause 15 of the Bill transfers this Regulation into the Act by inserting the new sections 45A and 45B, to allow the medical examination and surveillance of travellers entering or leaving Singapore.

sections.label: Clause 7 premises scope
sections.summary: Clause 7 inserts section 19A, incorporating Regulation 4 into the Act and expanding its scope beyond workplaces and dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 7 of the Bill inserts a new section 19A to incorporate the current Regulation 4 of the Infectious Diseases (Measures to Prevent or Control the Spread of Infectious Diseases) Regulations 2004 into the Act and expands its scope to include premises beyond workplaces and dormitories.

sections.label: Health advisories via operators
sections.summary: Clause 10 inserts section 21B to provide legal basis for using operators' capability and infrastructure to disseminate health advisories to specified persons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 10 of the Bill inserts a new section 21B, to provide the legal basis to tap on the capability, infrastructure and expertise of operators, to disseminate health advisories to persons specified in an order, such as persons travelling to or returning from overseas areas affected by an outbreak, or persons within or likely to enter any place within Singapore affected by or likely to be affected by an outbreak.

sections.label: Immunity for information disclosure
sections.summary: Clause 25 inserts section 67A granting immunity from legal liability to persons disclosing information in good faith under the IDA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In this regard, clause 25 of the Bill inserts a new section 67A, which confers immunity against legal liability under other laws, to persons disclosing or providing any information required under the IDA, in good faith and with reasonable care in accordance with any requirement under the Act.

sections.label: Health officers' enforcement measures
sections.summary: Clause 20 amends section 56 to let health officers use necessary measures, including physical means, to enforce legal orders, such as returning absconders to isolation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 20 of the Bill amends section 56 to allow health officers to take necessary measures, including the use of physical means, to enforce a legal order served under the Act, for example, by bringing an absconder back to the place of isolation, in lieu of arrest.

sections.label: Director's information sharing power
sections.summary: Clause 21 amends section 57A to empower the Director of Medical Services to share information without the Minister's approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To facilitate expedient information sharing, clause 21 of the Bill amends section 57A to empower the Director of Medical Services to do so, without the Minister's approval.

sections.label: Research use of information and samples
sections.summary: Clause 23 clarifies section 59A allows national public health research without imminent risk and amends it to permit use and sharing of information or samples for research.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 23 of the Bill, therefore, clarifies that section 59A allows national public health research to be conducted even when there is no imminent risk or crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 23 also amends section 59A, to allow the use of information or samples obtained through other sections of the Act for research, for example, surveillance or disease notification data, as well as to facilitate the use by my Ministry and sharing of individually-identifiable information or samples with third party researchers, where research can only be carried out using identifiable information or samples, for example, in tracing the transmission pathways and patterns of spread of a rare or new disease.

sections.label: Other amendments to the Act
sections.summary: Other amendments facilitate administration, including nomenclature alignment, ministerial responsibility clarification, seizure of records, and standard corporate liability provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There are also other amendments to the Act which facilitate its administration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These include alignment of nomenclature, firstly, for "Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection" and removal of "Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS)", a late stage subset of HIV; secondly, clarifying the responsibility of the Minister for Health and the Minister responsible for health and sanitary measures in relation to vessels, aircraft, vehicles and persons entering or leaving Singapore; thirdly, enabling the seizure of books, documents or records for investigation of offences, and the disposal of seized items; and lastly, the adoption of standard provisions on how liability for offences by corporations and other types of entities is to be determined.

sections.label: Risk-stratified outbreak management approaches
sections.summary: Risk-stratified approaches are to be put in place for managing outbreaks and infected and at-risk persons, given improved understanding of disease spread.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Second, to put in place risk-stratified approaches in managing outbreaks, and infected and at-risk persons, given our improved understanding of disease spread.

sections.label: Refusing entry to unvaccinated visitors
sections.summary: Unvaccinated non-citizen visitors from locations with active transmission of a serious communicable disease cannot be refused entry without first offering monitoring, prophylaxis or isolation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As the Senior Minister of State has just pointed out, presently, non-citizen visitors to Singapore travelling from a location with active transmission of a serious communicable disease, such as Yellow Fever, and who are unvaccinated and thus potential carriers of the disease, cannot be refused entry without first offering them monitoring, disease prophylaxis or isolation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I agree with the Ministry that this can be impractical, particularly if the numbers of visitors arriving are large, and many countries already reserve the right to turn away unvaccinated travellers.

sections.label: Risk stratification of cases and carriers
sections.summary: Amended section 21 allows risk stratification of disease cases and carriers for limited vocational duties or limited travel outside their homes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, the amended section 21 now allows for risk stratification of disease cases and carriers, so that they may perform limited vocational duties, or make limited travel outside their homes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For cases and carriers, I would like to ask what is the mechanism by which they can appeal for or against that particular risk classification.

sections.label: Monitoring and reporting infectious diseases
sections.summary: Steps are needed to monitor and implement measures controlling infectious diseases, with doctors and laboratories required to report detections to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, we need to take steps to closely monitor and implement measures on how infectious diseases can be controlled to protect the health of our local population.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that there are various requirements for doctors and those who run laboratories carrying out various medical tests to report to MOH when infectious diseases are detected.

sections.label: Disseminating health advisories and entry returns
sections.summary: Under new section 21B the Minister can seek assistance from mobile and transport operators to disseminate health advisories, and section 31 allows Port Health Officers to return certain persons.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How do we help educate them about their social responsibility towards the community?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that MOH, under a new section 21B, the Minister can seek the assistance of mobile operators as well as various transport operators to disseminate health advisories.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I feel that MOH may also tap on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' (MFA's) website and app to disseminate such health measures to be taken for Singaporeans who register with MFA before they travel abroad, especially to high health-risk countries.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that section 31 allows the Port Health Officer to return a person, who is not a Singapore citizen, who arrives in Singapore without having undergone a vaccination or prophylaxis.

sections.label: Audit of airport trays
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOH conducted any audit of the trays at the airport and other checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Did MOH do any such audit of the trays at our airport and other checkpoints?

sections.label: Disinfecting contacts of infectious patients
sections.summary: The passage says places an infectious patient contacted, such as aircraft cabins, security trays and taxis, should be disinfected to prevent virus spread.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although it is good that patients with infectious diseases can be deported, the various places he has been in contact with, such as the aircraft cabin, the security screen trays and the taxis, should also be disinfected accordingly to prevent the spread of viruses.

sections.label: AMR deaths worldwide
sections.summary: A Singapore-MIT Alliance study shows AMR causes about 700,000 deaths yearly worldwide, predicted to reach 10 million yearly by 2050, outpacing cancer mortality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A study from the Singapore-Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Alliance for Research and Technology shows that AMR currently results in about 700,000 deaths per year worldwide, with recent studies predicting an increase to 10 million deaths per year by 2050, outpacing the mortality of cancer.

sections.label: AMR costs and antibiotic development
sections.summary: AMR is predicted to cost up to S$130 trillion by 2050, and a WHO report says only 11 antibiotics in clinical development address critical pathogens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On a global scale, AMR is predicted to cost up to S$130 trillion by 2050." These statistics are very distressing and not at all encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a WHO report, only 11 antibiotics in clinical development could address pathogens considered critical threats, and three in four of the antibiotics under development belong to existing classes of antibiotics, against which microbials resistance has already been observed or could easily develop, due to the innovative nature of these "superbugs" in evading our current controls.

sections.label: Antibiotic framework in community
sections.summary: Public hospitals have systems to curb antibiotic misuse and overuse, but a similar framework is needed in the community, where private practices provide 80% of primary healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, we have systems in public hospitals to curb the misuse and overuse of antibiotics, but we will require a similar framework in the community where 80% of the primary healthcare is provided by private practices.

sections.label: MediSave flu vaccination claims
sections.summary: Flu vaccinations are currently claimable by MediSave for specific population groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Flu vaccinations are currently claimable by MediSave for specific population groups.

sections.label: Returns from health protection interventions
sections.summary: According to the review, health protection interventions, including vaccinations matching the actual influenza type, have saved $34 for every $1 spent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Health protection interventions, which would include vaccinations that match the actual influenza type, have saved $34 for every $1 spent on them, according to the review.

sections.label: Clostridium difficile antibiotic-related infection
sections.summary: Clostridium difficile infects the bowels and causes diarrhoea, is usually related to antibiotic use, particularly in hospitals, and caused an estimated 14,000 US deaths annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clostridium difficile, a bacterium which infects the bowels and causes diarrhoea, is one such example of an infection usually related to antibiotic use, particularly in hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It has been responsible for an estimated 14,000 deaths annually in the US.

sections.label: Support for Infectious Diseases amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendment Bill, noting the Infectious Diseases Bill was first enacted in 1977 and last amended in 2008.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my proposal and concerns above, I stand to support the amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Infectious Diseases Bill was first enacted in 1977 and last amended in 2008.

sections.label: Chain of command in outbreak
sections.summary: The passage asks what chain of command Singapore practises in light of an infectious disease outbreak or suspected outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One, in light of an infectious disease outbreak or suspected outbreak in Singapore, what is the chain of command that we practise?

sections.label: Cross-border outbreak working with neighbours
sections.summary: The passage asks how and what Singapore's model of working and communications with closest neighbours, such as Malaysia, will be in a cross-border outbreak or spread.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, in the event of cross-border outbreak or spread, how and what will be our model of working and communications with our closest neighbours, for example, Malaysia?

sections.label: Persons on flights to Singapore
sections.summary: The passage asks about persons on flights enroute to Singapore who are suspected or diagnosed with certain infectious diseases.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Fifth, what about persons on flights enroute to Singapore who are suspected or are diagnosed with certain infectious diseases?

sections.label: Changi Airport flights and passengers
sections.summary: About 7,200 flights land or depart from Changi Airport each week, and as at November last year approximately 60 million passengers passed through in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: About 7,200 flights land or depart from Changi Airport each week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As at November last year, approximately 60 million passengers passed through Changi Airport in 2018.

sections.label: Amendment to Section 21
sections.summary: Section 21 of the Act is proposed to be amended to let the Government take a more calibrated approach to address infectious disease spread by carriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Section 21 of the Act is proposed to be amended to allow the Government to take a more calibrated approach to address the risk of the spread of infectious diseases by persons who are carrying infectious diseases.

sections.label: Relief from contractual obligations
sections.summary: It suggests considering a statutory basis to relieve people from liability for contractual business or trade obligations while directed to act, rendering them unable to perform work obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Even if we do not go so far as to compensate people in respect of stop-work directions given, perhaps we can at least consider having a statutory basis for people to be relieved or held harmless from liability for their contractual business or trade obligations for the period that they are directed by the Director to do an act which renders them unable to perform their work obligations.

sections.label: Prescribed infectious diseases list scope
sections.summary: It asks whether the prescribed infectious diseases list applies only to section 6, and notes MOH received WHO plaudits for detecting and preventing disease spread.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Or is it contemplated that the application of the prescribed infectious diseases list is only in respect of section 6 of the Act, since no other sections of the Act refers to prescribed infectious diseases?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He mentioned that MOH received plaudits from WHO for its ability to successfully detect and prevent the spread of infectious diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is a hard-earned reputation and, frankly, whatever we pass today in the House, it is the capability of MOH and its professionals that would make a decisive difference in the fight against the spread of infectious diseases.

sections.label: Director's power to cease occupation
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to confirm the Director will not have blanket power to order a person to cease their occupation, trade or business indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that the Director will not have the blanket power to order a person to cease their occupation, trade or business for an indefinite period?

sections.label: Time period limited by reasonableness
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to confirm whether any time period specified will at least be limited by the requirement of reasonableness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm whether any time period specified will at least be limited by the requirement of reasonableness?

sections.label: Notification of disclosure
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to clarify whether the affected person will be notified of the disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether the affected person will be notified of the disclosure?

sections.label: Feedback on proposed amendments
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to share key feedback on the proposed amendments and whether any responses were accepted in drafting the final Bill, including discretion to turn back unvaccinated travellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the key feedback that was received on the proposed amendments, and whether any of the responses were accepted by the Ministry in drafting this final Bill?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the proposals is the discretion to turn back unvaccinated travellers.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger numbers
sections.summary: Changi Airport has about 60 million passengers passing through it each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Changi Airport has about 60 million passengers passing through it each year.

sections.label: New devices and technologies
sections.summary: The question asks whether new devices and technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence will be tapped, noting a German research project, HyFly, to prevent airports from being infection gateways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, will we be tapping on new devices and technologies, such as big data and artificial intelligence?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that there is a German research project, HyFly, underway to prevent airports from being gateways for infection.

sections.label: Health advisories dissemination requirement
sections.summary: The Bill requires mobile and transport operators and persons in charge of premises to disseminate health advisories to prevent disease transmission.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another key amendment is the legislative requirement for mobile and transport operators and persons in charge of premises to disseminate health advisories as part of prevention of disease transmission.

sections.label: Medical examinations and surveillance
sections.summary: The Bill allows a person to be subjected to medical examinations over a period of time and placed under medical surveillance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill also allows for a person to be subjected to medical examinations over a period of time and be placed under medical surveillance.

sections.label: Stop-work orders for professions
sections.summary: The Director of Medical Services may direct persons in professions likely to spread infectious diseases to stop their occupation, and the Ministry is asked to consider specifying a maximum period for such orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Director of Medical Services is also allowed to direct persons involved in professions that are deemed to likely cause the spread of any infectious diseases to stop carrying on with their occupation, trade or business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry consider specifying a maximum period of days for such a stop-work order, so that businesses can take this into account as part of their emergency preparedness plans?

sections.label: Fund for affected workers
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider setting up a fund to mitigate the impact on this group of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider setting up a fund that would help mitigate such an impact for this group of workers?

sections.label: Amendments to the IDA
sections.summary: The proposed IDA amendments aim to keep legislative tools relevant and let Singapore respond to current and future infectious disease threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the IDA are to ensure that our legislative tools remain relevant and allow Singapore to adequately respond to both current and future infectious diseases threats.

sections.label: Clause 10 inserting section 21B
sections.summary: Clause 10, by inserting section 21B, enables the Ministry to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Clause 10, in inserting section 21B, enables my Ministry to do so.

sections.label: Clause 15 medical examination transfer
sections.summary: Clause 15 transfers the subsidiary regulation for medical examination of persons entering Singapore to section 45A, strengthening prevention of infectious disease import.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Clause 15, in transferring the subsidiary regulation that allows for the medical examination of persons entering Singapore to section 45A of the Act, strengthens the ability of my Ministry to prevent the import of infectious diseases.

sections.label: Section 31 disease scope
sections.summary: Section 31 applies only to diseases with vaccination or prophylaxis, such as Yellow Fever, not emerging diseases without such measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked whether section 31 of the Bill applies to emerging infectious diseases with no preventive or therapeutic measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I wish to clarify that section 31 only applies to diseases that have vaccination or prophylaxis, such as Yellow Fever.

sections.label: Ministry horizon scanning framework
sections.summary: The Ministry uses its own framework, horizon scanning and public health principles to monitor risks to Singapore and calibrate responses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: While we take reference from the recommendations of international bodies and respected public health authorities, we must also have our own framework to monitor and identify risks to Singapore and calibrate our responses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: My Ministry performs horizon scanning of disease situations around the world, and assesses the risk to Singapore, based on public health principles.

sections.label: National AMR action plan framework
sections.summary: Singapore's National Strategic Action Plan on AMR sets the framework for the national response among key Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Singapore's National Strategic Action Plan on AMR sets the framework for the national response among key Government agencies.

sections.label: Salmonella notification by laboratories
sections.summary: The Act allows the Ministry to prescribe Salmonella as an infectious disease to be notified by laboratories but not medical practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In this case, the Act allows the Ministry to prescribe Salmonella as an infectious disease to be notified by laboratories but not the medical practitioners.

sections.label: SARS ex-gratia payments
sections.summary: During the 2003 SARS outbreak, the Government provided ex-gratia payments to eligible persons on home quarantine orders and employees of small businesses ordered to shut.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: During the SARS outbreak in 2003, the Government provided ex-gratia payments to eligible persons on home quarantine orders and employees of small businesses which were ordered to be shut.

sections.label: Managers assist contact tracing
sections.summary: Clause 7, in inserting section 19A, allows the Ministry to enlist the assistance of managers of premises to conduct contact tracing and surveillance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Clause 7, in inserting section 19A, allows my Ministry to enlist the assistance of managers of premises to conduct contact tracing and surveillance.
